영어(en): The Elite Rule requires precise defense.#The closer you time a Receive or Slide to the moment the player touches the ball, the more accurate it is. Accuracy determines whether you receive a PERFECT, GREAT, GOOD, or BAD rating.#The closer the rating is to PERFECT, the less damage your Individual Stamina and Mental take.

A Perfect Defense performed within the required frame window counters 100% of the opposing attack and nullifies special abilities.#A Perfect Receive delivers an A Pass and restores some Individual Stamina and Mental.#Receive: within 1 frame#Slide: within 3 frames
GREAT Defense counters 80% of the opposing attack.#If Individual Stamina is too low, the defense may fail even with a GREAT rating.

Defending too late may result in a BAD rating. BAD Defense increases the damage to the defending player’s Individual Stamina and Mental, so it is best to avoid a BAD Receive rating.#When Sliding, you will not receive a BAD Defense rating.

Under the Elite Rule, press the Receive button to command when your teammates receive.#If no command is given before the receive window ends, teammates defend on their own at the last possible moment.#The defense timing gauge shows the accuracy of your commands or your teammates’ automatic decisions.

Players who lose all of their Mental enter the Exhausted state.#While Exhausted, Individual Stamina and Mental do not recover.#Exhaustion can be removed by substituting the player or calling a timeout, and when it is removed, both Mental and Individual Stamina are fully recovered.
Each player has their own Mental. When it runs out, they become Exhausted.#Mental decreases in proportion to the Power of the opposing attack, but Defense can reduce the damage.
Each player has their own Stamina. When it is low, the ball will bounce far away even if they Receive or Slide to defend an opposing attack.
